brief: Goldman's European equity sales daily reports a risk-off tape: the S&P fell 71bps to 7631 on Iran headlines, inflation fears and higher yields, with Brent back to $95, US and Bund 10yr at 4.80% and 3.34%, Japan's 10yr above 3% for the first time since 1996, and markets pricing a 66% probability of a September Fed hike. US strikes on Iranian targets and Tehran's missile response are given as the driver. European gas above €70/MWh, higher than 2022, supports a basket of gas-consuming companies expected to underperform against a long in power-price-sensitive utilities. Dell beat and raised F2027 guidance on AI server demand, lifting its AI server revenue outlook to $74bn from $60bn and total revenue to $192bn, so Goldman raises F2027-29 EPS by 38% on average and keeps Buy with a $425 target. It stays constructive on European equities at 14.5x earnings and a 5.3% free cash flow yield, and upgrades Deutsche Bank to Buy on a roughly 300bps return-on-tangible-equity improvement over three years. Bitcoin ETF inflows broke a nine-session streak and the CLARITY Act faces a procedural floor vote on 15 September.
